overview.en: Cairo layers medieval streets, major museums and busy Nile-side neighborhoods into an intense city break. Explore its monuments on foot, leave time for the markets, and experience a city whose cafes and social life carry on well into the evening.
overview.ar: القاهرة فيها أكتر من حكاية في نفس المشوار: شوارع قديمة ومتاحف كبيرة وقعدات على النيل وأسواق لسه عايشة بطريقتها. خصصلها وقت للمشي والاستكشاف، وسيب مساحة لقعدة قهوة أو لفة بالليل بعيد عن جدول المزارات.

history.en: The Fatimid city of al-Qahira was founded in 969. Its Islamic and Coptic landmarks, medieval commercial streets and later Downtown buildings reveal several different periods of the city's history.

photos.description: Mohamed Ali Mosque، The mosque is distinguished by its marble cladding; its interior and exterior walls, up to a height of 11 meters, are covered with alabaster marble quarried in Wadi Sannur, Beni Suef. For this reason, the mosque is also known as the "Alabaster Mosque." The mosque's outer courtyard features an ornate copper clock tower, a gift from King Louis Philippe of France to Muhammad Ali Pasha in 1845, in return for Muhammad Ali's gift of the Luxor Obelisk, which stands in the Place de la Concorde in Paris. In the southwestern corner of the mosque lies the mausoleum of Muhammad Ali Pasha, a marble structure carved from the distinctive white Italian Carrara marble. His remains were moved from their original burial place in Hawsh al-Basha to this mausoleum in 1857 by order of his son, Said Pasha.

overview.en: Alexandria combines a Mediterranean waterfront with Greek, Roman and later Egyptian heritage. Its library, gardens, old neighborhoods and seafood restaurants make a different kind of city break from Cairo.
overview.ar: إسكندرية ليها إيقاع تاني: بحر ومشي وأكل سمك، ومعاهم تاريخ يوناني وروماني وأحياء كل واحدة بطابعها. بين المكتبة والحدايق والآثار، تقدر تعمل زيارة ثقافية وتسيب وقت للبحر من غير استعجال.

history.en: Alexander the Great founded Alexandria in 331 BC. It became a major center of learning and culture in the ancient Mediterranean, a legacy recalled by today's Bibliotheca Alexandrina.
history.ar: الإسكندر الأكبر أسس المدينة سنة 331 قبل الميلاد، وبعدها بقت مركز مهم للعلم والثقافة في العالم القديم. مكتبة الإسكندرية الحالية بتستحضر الحكاية دي بشكل معاصر.

geography.en: The governorate sits on Egypt's Mediterranean coast west of the Nile Delta. Coastal weather is wetter in winter than the Nile Valley's southern cities.

overview.en: Luxor brings the monumental landscape of ancient Thebes into everyday view. The Nile divides major east-bank temples from the west-bank royal tombs and funerary temples, making the river itself part of the visit.

photos.description: Aerial view during sunrise of the Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut , Luxor , Egypt. The mortuary temple built during the reign of Pharaoh Hatshepsut of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt . The temple is considered to be a masterpiece of ancient architecture. Its three massive terraces rise above the desert floor and into the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari . Her tomb, KV20 , lies inside the same massif capped by El Qurn , a pyramid for her mortuary complex. Across the river Nile , the whole structure points towards the monumental Eighth Pylon, Hatshepsut's most recognizable addition to the Temple of Karnak and the site from which the procession of the Beautiful Festival of the Valley departed.

overview.en: The Red Sea Governorate combines coral-fringed coast, resort towns and the Eastern Desert. Hurghada and El Gouna offer established visitor infrastructure, while Marsa Alam and Wadi El Gemal open up a different coastal and desert landscape farther south.

history.en: Hurghada grew from a fishing settlement into an international tourism center. The governorate's identity is not limited to modern resorts: its coastal ports and desert routes connect it to a much longer regional history.

geography.en: This mainland governorate lies between the Nile Valley and the Red Sea. Do not confuse it with the wider tourism region: Sharm el-Sheikh and Dahab are in South Sinai, and Ain Sokhna is in Suez.

overview.en: South Sinai combines coral reefs, Bedouin communities and high granite mountains. Sharm el-Sheikh, laid-back Dahab and the religious landscape around Saint Catherine offer very different experiences within one governorate.

photos.description: "the Benevolent Bridges") is a city in Qalyubia Governorate, Egypt. It is the location of the Delta Barrages, the first modern irrigation structure across the Nile, located at the apex of the Nile Delta. In the mid 1850s, when Viceroy Sa'id Pasha took over project construction he ordered a silver medal to be struck to mark the occasion. He then ordered the construction of a town near the incomplete barrage. Again the project would be bogged down due to financial problems; the original barrages were initially completed in 1862, and greatly improved in the 1880s under British rule. A new barrage structure was built slightly downstream in 1939.[1] The name of the city, is a reference to the structure and the river crossing it nonetheless provided.

photos.description: Sannur Cave extends for about 700 metres. Fifteen metres wide and 15 metres deep, it consists mainly of limestone overlaid with alabaster created by thermal springs in the middle Eocene period about 60 million years ago. Its unique geological formations, known as stalactites and stalagmites, formed beautifully over millions of years. The importance of this cave is due to the rarity of these natural formations in Egypt

overview.en: New Valley is the governorate of great Western Desert distances: Kharga, Dakhla and Farafra are separate oasis worlds rather than adjoining neighborhoods. Historic mud-brick settlements, temples and the White Desert make careful route planning essential.
overview.ar: الوادي الجديد محافظة المسافات الصحراوية الكبيرة؛ الخارجة والداخلة والفرافرة كل واحة فيهم عالم لوحده، مش أماكن جنب بعض. القرى القديمة والمعابد والصحراء البيضاء محتاجين تخطيط طريق على مهل.

history.en: Oasis temples and settlements preserve ancient Egyptian, Persian-period, Roman and later histories. The modern governorate's name is linked to the New Valley development project.
history.ar: معابد الواحات ومستوطناتها بتحفظ تاريخ مصري قديم وفارسي وروماني وفترات بعدهم. واسم المحافظة الحديث مرتبط بمشروع الوادي الجديد.

geography.en: Egypt's largest governorate by area lies in the southwestern Western Desert; its capital is Kharga.
geography.ar: أكبر محافظات مصر مساحة، في جنوب غرب الصحراء الغربية، وعاصمتها الخارجة.

overview.en: Matrouh stretches from Mediterranean beach towns to the inland oasis of Siwa. Marsa Matrouh, El Alamein and Siwa belong to one governorate but need different seasons, routes and expectations.
overview.ar: مطروح ممتدة من مدن وشواطئ المتوسط لحد واحة سيوة جوه الصحرا. مرسى مطروح والعلمين وسيوة تبع محافظة واحدة، لكن كل مكان فيهم محتاج موسم وطريق وتوقعات مختلفة.

history.en: El Alamein preserves the memory of major Second World War battles. Siwa adds a much older oasis history, including the oracle associated with Alexander the Great.
history.ar: العلمين بتحفظ ذاكرة معارك كبيرة في الحرب العالمية التانية. وسيوة ليها تاريخ واحات أقدم بكتير، ومنه معبد الوحي المرتبط بزيارة الإسكندر الأكبر.

geography.en: A large northwestern governorate along the Mediterranean and Libya border, extending deep into the Western Desert.
